— Occupant Safety and Distraction Elimination","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Occupant Safety and Distraction Elimination

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Blind spots hide beyond mirror reach and grow from gear like posts and mirrors plus scenery like trees, sun, hedges, hills, and walls [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Refuse to cruise in another driver's blind spot by speeding up or dropping back, and hurry through it when passing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
Never pace a truck or bus, whose giant blind zones can swallow your car unseen [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Learn your own car's natural blind zones and treat every lane change and cross-traffic pullout as a blind-spot check [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
Weather and daylight swell blind spots, with windshield sun glare the worst offender, so deploy sunglasses or visors against it [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
Buckle every soul before rolling, since crashes top teen killers and belting up is the cheapest escape from that count [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A01
Cinched lap belts ride snug on hips, and expectant mothers wear them low across the pelvis beneath the belly [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A01
Beltless driving is a primary stoppable offense fining up to $50 per rider and $100 per rider under 18 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A01
Belts rank as the top lifesaver in crashes, and Iowa law demands them for every front-seat rider plus every backseat rider under 18 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A02
Babies under one year and under 20 pounds ride only in rear-facing restraints [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A02
Children under six ride only in child restraints, meaning safety or booster seats and never a bare belt [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A02
Children six through seventeen ride restrained or belted in every seat, front and back [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A02
No one under 18 may ride in the open bed of a moving pickup [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A02
Adults eighteen and up must belt in front seats [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A02
Survivors stay inside: belts stop ejection into the path of other cars, beating the thrown-clear fantasy [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A02
Belt choice affects all: loose riders turn projectile, and a lone loose driver can be flung from the seat into a crash [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A02
Town trips kill too: over half of traffic deaths strike within 25 miles of home, many on roads under 45 mph [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A02
Belts free in under a second, and by keeping you conscious through fire or water crashes they improve escape odds [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A02
Strap down cabin cargo: at 60 mph a 20-pound object can slam with over 1,000 pounds of force [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A02
Sweep floors clear so nothing rolls beneath the brake pedal and steals your brakes [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A03
Distraction splits three ways: visual eyes-off like GPS glances, manual hands-off like eating or makeup, and cognitive mind-off like music or chat [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A03
Every distraction type endangers, and everyday wheel tasks often stack two or three at once [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A03
Iowa bans writing, sending, or viewing electronic messages while driving; texts, emails, and posts wait until you halt fully off the traveled road [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A03
The message ban spares on-duty public safety crews, emergency healthcare acts, and incoming safety, traffic, and weather alerts [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A03
Drivers under 18 holding permits, intermediate, or special minor licenses may not call or talk while driving short of a full off-road stop [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A03
Distracted driving is a primary pull-over offense risking fines plus license or permit suspension or loss [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A03
Distracted killing brings fines past $1,000, license suspension, and possible vehicular homicide charges [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A03
Hands-free law bans holding the phone, manual scrolling or typing, GPS address entry, video streaming or calls even by voice, viewing texts, videos, or social feeds, and any calling or dialing outside hands-free or voice control [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A03
Covered electronic devices span cell phones, PDAs, tablets, gaming devices, and laptops [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0036]

Misconceptions: staying inside the car beats being thrown clear; an unbuckled rider endangers everyone as a projectile; short town trips still host most deadly crashes.

Mnemonic: eyes, hands, mind are the three distraction thieves; buckle all, face rear the tiny, hands free the phone.

Glossary: blind spot (an area mirrors cannot show); primary offense (a stoppable violation on its own); child restraint system (a safety or booster seat, not a belt); hands-free (voice-only device use with no holding or touching).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every safety and distraction rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
